methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective observational cohort study with 221 subjects (74 healthy controls, 78 lung cancer, 69 LC with brain metastasis). Groups well-defined by pathology and MRI criteria. Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) provides quantitative parameters (Ktrans, Kep, Ve, Vp) with standardized imaging protocol (3T scanner, specific flip angles, TR/TE reported). Post-processing uses Extended Tofts two-compartment model with explicit methodology. Statistical analysis includes normality testing (Kolmogorov-Smirnov), appropriate tests (Mann-Whitney U, Spearman correlation), p<0.05 significance threshold.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Investigates blood-brain barrier abnormalities in non-brain-metastatic lung cancer, proposing biomarkers for brain metastasis risk stratification. Directly relevant to neuroprotective strategies and prediction of metastatic progression. Findings could inform individualized surveillance and therapeutic approaches (VEGF/MMP inhibitors, BBB protectants, radiotherapy planning).

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive reporting of imaging methodology: scanner model, sequence parameters (flip angles, matrix, FOV, TR/TE, temporal resolution), contrast agent administration protocol. Post-processing explicitly described (motion correction, ROI delineation >150mm²). Results organized by white matter regions with statistical comparisons. Figures effectively display regional differences. No statement regarding image/raw data availability from hospital database.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel application of quantitative DCE-MRI to characterize pre-metastatic white matter microenvironment in lung cancer. First to demonstrate regional and histopathological subtype-specific BBB abnormalities (ADC: global leakage via hyperperfusion; SCLC: interstitial disruption in deep white matter). Fills gap between prior diffusion tensor imaging studies and mechanistic understanding.

writing_presentation.justification: Excellent organization with detailed Introduction establishing white matter importance and research gap. Methods meticulously describe imaging protocol, image processing, statistical approaches. Results clearly presented with figures showing regional comparisons and subtype differences. Discussion comprehensively contextualizes findings within prior neuroimaging literature and proposes clinical applications (threshold values, surveillance intervals).

key_strengths: Novel quantitative imaging biomarkers for brain metastasis risk stratification in lung cancer
Rigorous DCE-MRI methodology with explicit imaging parameters enabling reproducibility
Subtype-specific findings (ADC: Ktrans 33 min-1/1000; SCLC: Ve 10.60/1000) with mechanistic rationale
Clinical actionable thresholds proposed (Ktrans >22, Ve >10/1000 as warning levels)
key_concerns: Retrospective design with single-center enrollment; selection bias from CNS disease cohort not fully addressed
Modest sample size (78 LC, 69 LCBM) limits subgroup analyses; rare lung cancer subtypes excluded
Mechanistic inference (VEGF-mediated, neuroinflammatory) based on imaging correlates; lacks direct molecular evidence
No clinical outcome validation; threshold values proposed but not prospectively tested for predictive value
Data availability not stated; inability to access imaging data limits external validation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 2 paper: novel imaging biomarkers with sound methodology and significant clinical potential. Proposes actionable risk stratification tool for brain metastasis prevention. Appropriate for high-tier oncology/neurooncology imaging journals; minor revisions to add mechanistic evidence (CSF markers, molecular validation) and prospective validation plan.
